question: If 40% of first number is equal to two-sevenths of second number, what is the ratio of first number to the second number?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert 40% directly to its simplified fraction value: 40% = 2/5

Equate the fractional parts of both numbers: (2/5) × I = (2/7) × II

Cancel out the common numerator 2 from both sides of the equation.

I / II = 5 / 7 ⇒ I : II = 5 : 7

**∴ The correct answer is 5 : 7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

40% of the first number is equal to 2/7 of the second number.

 
 40% of 1st
 =
 
 2/7 of 2nd
 

 

 2/5 × 1st
 2/7 × 2nd

**Calculations:**

Let the first number be x and the second number be y.

⇒ 40% of x = 2/7 of y

⇒ (40 / 100) × x = (2 / 7) × y

⇒ (2 / 5) × x = (2 / 7) × y

⇒ x / y = (2 / 7) ÷ (2 / 5)

⇒ x / y = (2 / 7) × (5 / 2)

⇒ x / y = 5 / 7

⇒ x : y = 5 : 7

**∴ The correct answer is 5 : 7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage to Fraction Conversion

Knowing standard conversion equivalents saves calculation time during exams: 20% = 1/5, 40% = 2/5, 60% = 3/5, 80% = 4/5.

Ratio and Proportion

A ratio simply indicates how many times one number contains another. If a/b = c/d, the ratio of a to b is the same as c to d, represented standardly as a : b :: c : d.

Cross-Multiplication Principle

When comparing or equating two fractions a/b = c/d, you can apply cross-multiplication to rapidly solve for unknown variables: a × d = b × c.
